items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: The interviewee narrates a story about drummer Debo Mills and his wife Anna May Winburn, stating 'this was his wife' and describing a recording session involving Debo Mills singing lyrics to Anna May. The interviewee (Horace Henderson) does not claim a personal relationship with Anna May Winburn, on

ctx.x: band. He also liked Emmett Barry, the great trumpet player. Well, John Hammond had me get Israel Crosby, Emmet Barry, and myself together. We flew out to Omaha, Nebraska, and -- I hate to say it -- we raided Nat Towles' band because he wasn't doing too much, but they could play, man. They were together. But we stayed in Omaha about two weeks, and I rehearsed in a house there where I was staying. John Hammond financed us this whole thing for me, and we got together and rehearsed, and he flew us to New York City to…

There was an all girl revue band called the International Sweethearts of Rhythm. Well, the leader of this particular band was a girl named Anna May Winburn. Well, this was his wife, and -- I'm saying this to say that we made a recording in New York, and he sang also, and he sang some lyrics to Anna May, you know. It was a blues. It was a great thing, and the record sold pretty good.

But John Hammond, getting back to what he did for us, he came out to Omaha after I had kept him, you know, well -- what shall I say -- he wanted to know, let's put it this way, what was going on, and so after two weeks of rehearsing I was keeping him -- what's the word I want?
